correctness.rationale: On distinct basis vectors the Leibniz identity equates scalar multiples of two nonzero 0–1 neighborhood vectors. For different supports the two scalars vanish, whereas identical supports give symmetric off-diagonal entries in characteristic two. Thus D is block-diagonal on open twin classes. The square identities give D(e_i^2)=0; each neighborhood is a union of whole twin classes, their block supports are disjoint, and every class occurs in some neighborhood. Hence each block kills its all-ones vector. These basis identities are also sufficient by bilinearity. The self-adjoint idempotents for the nondegenerate dot product on a block are in bijection with their nondegenerate images via projection along the orthogonal complement. Killing the ones vector places the image in H=1^perp, where the dot product is alternating because B(x,x)=(sum x_i)^2. In odd block size H is symplectic; in even size its radical is the line of ones and the quotient is symplectic, each with symplectic dimension 2h in the relevant space. Nondegenerate subspaces of H have zero intersection with the radical; each rank-2r quotient subspace has exactly q^(2r) distinct complements to the radical in its inverse image, counted by differences of linear sections. The symplectic group is transitive on the nondegenerate rank-2r subspaces with stabilizer Sp(2r) times Sp(2h−2r); dividing group orders gives q^(2r(h−r)) times the Gaussian binomial with base q^2. This yields the parity-dependent coefficient and a product over independently selected blocks. Symplectic bases and linear sections also give all even ranks over arbitrary characteristic-two fields, including the cases a=1,2 with h=0; the sums of the block rank intervals have no omitted even rank. Fresh row-span enumeration in F2 through size six corroborates the small coefficients independently of the supplied matrix enumeration; it is not the arbitrary-dimensional proof.
residual_risks: Connected simple graphs with at least two vertices and characteristic two only; the enumerator requires a finite field. A compositional idempotent linear derivation need not be an algebra retraction.

originality.rationale: The general derivation-space normal form and its dependence on the twin partition are already essentially supplied by Reis–Cadavid. Symplectic subspace counts are standard. The distinct conclusion is the exact rank census for the nonlinear idempotence constraint in this specific derivation space, including the even-class radical-lift factor and the complete product for arbitrary open twin sizes; not the derivation-space block classification or a new counting theorem about symplectic spaces alone.
residual_risks: The finite literature and index comparisons do not establish world priority; an unindexed formula for this precise class could overlap. The standard symplectic count is reconstructed rather than claimed as new.

value.rationale: Composition-idempotent derivations measure the possible two-summand splittings of the underlying vector space selected by a Leibniz operator, which the linear derivation space alone does not quantify. The result gives every rank and its exact labeled multiplicity over every finite even field for a natural family, and detects a genuine odd/even twin-size difference in counts via a radical line. This is a complete nonlinear invariant not supplied by the known linear classification.
residual_risks: It is not a new classification of all derivations, nor does it count projections modulo conjugacy or in odd characteristic.
